Set the distance to the zero parallax point. Decrease this value to increase the toe-in angle.
Set the distance between stereo cameras.

Set the type of eye separation falloff model. Use 'None' to keep  the same eye separation along all latitude values. Use 'Linear' to set a linear decay starting at the given start falloff angle value. Use 'Cosine' to set a cosine decay according to the given exponent. Use 'Sigmoid' to set a sigmoid decay minimising the falloff area at the poles.

impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.
Interpolate between keyframes of animation during the shutter apperture.It can cause deviation from the motion, but it can help to decrease the number keyframes and stochastic samples needed.

The projection modes are:
Perspective: Objects in front of the camera have the illusion of depth defined by the camera's focal-length and aperture.
Orthographic: Objects are viewed using a parallel projection.
SphericalMap: The entire 360deg world is rendered as a spherical map. Render Camera: Take the projection mode from the camera.

Set the diameter of the camera rig used to generate a corresponding stereoscopic image stitch. Use 'Sample rays from camera radius' to sample rays from the radius defined by this rig size so that the render matches the image stitch.The diameter should be bigger than the eye separation.
Set the output right view.
Sample rays with respect to the capture radius for a camera rig. Select this to match stereoscopic image stitches generated for a horizontal ring of cameras.
Number of keyframes used to reconstruct motion blur during the shutter aperture.

Set the rate of fall-off for the eye separation towards the poles. This defines the exponent of a cosine function. Set the exponent to one to get a smooth merging of depth at the poles between left and right view. Reduce the exponent to shift the transition in depth toward the poles. Set the falloff to zero to prevent pole merging.
Set the starting angle for linear fall-off in the eye separation towards the poles. Increase the angle to shift the start point for fall-off towards the poles. Set this to 90 to prevent pole merging.
This is how long the shutter should be open for when motion blurring. The value is in frames, so 0.5 is half a frame.

If the shutteroffset parameter is set to 'custom', this parameter is used to set the time that the shutter opens by adding it to the current frame.

Values are in frames, so -0.5 would open the shutter half a frame before the current frame.

The value of this controls how the shutter behaves with respect to the current frame value. It has four options
  • centred - centres the shutter around the frame, ie: open from f - shutter/2 to f + shutter/2
  • start - opens the shutter starting at the frame, ie: open from f to f + shutter
  • end - closes the shutter at the frame, ie: open from f - shutter to f
  • custom - opens the shutter at the time specified by the shuttercustomoffset parameter.
Stereo Scan Enable

Number of samples per pixel to use in stochastic estimation. Zero disables stochastic sampling. It is recommended for motion blur that the number of scenes to sample (samples knob) is adjusted. This will also provide anti-aliasing by jittering the sample point.
Set the error tolerance in the triangle-ray intersection calculations.
Use a uniform temporal distribution of scenes to samples.This generates more accurate results for stochastic multisampling.
If using a single sample, always use a zero shutter offset unless a custom one is specified. This matches the behaviour of ScanlineRender.

RayRender

'obj/scn' input: (required) Scene containing objects or an individual object to be rendered.

When connected to a Scene all the objects and lights connected to that scene will be rendered.

'cam' input: (optional) Viewing camera. If the camera input is not connected, the renderer will use a default camera positioned at the origin and facing in the negative Z direction.

'bg' input: (optional) Determines the output format and background. If not used, will default to root.format or root.proxy_format.
